[EVENT] User received a new tennis racket today.  
[PREFERENCE] User is excited to try out new techniques with their tennis racket.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant congratulated the user on their new tennis racket and provided tips to improve their serve.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for improving tennis serves include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Grip: Use the continental grip.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Stance: Feet shoulder-width apart, body facing the net, weight on the back foot.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Toss: Toss the ball 6-8 feet in the air, 6-8 inches in front of the body, slightly to the right.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Racket position: Hold the racket at a 90-degree angle to the body.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Contact: Make contact at the peak of the toss, with a slightly closed racket face.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Follow-through: Keep the racket close to the body.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Body rotation: Rotate the body to generate power.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Variation: Mix up serves (flat, topspin, slice).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Practice: Regular practice to develop muscle memory.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Film yourself serving to analyze technique.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips for the new racket include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Get familiar with the racket's sweet spot.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Adjust to the racket's power level.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Experiment with different strings.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant reminded the user that improving their serve takes time and practice.
